name: Landfill Disposals Tax Communities Scheme
summary: Welsh Government grants, run by WCVA, for community projects within five miles of eligible waste sites. One of the three themes is biodiversity: building resilient ecological networks for habitats and species.

geography.label: Wales, within five miles of eligible waste sites

amount.note: Plus one nationally significant project a year of £50,000 to £250,000

eligibility.rule: Be an incorporated body based in and operating for the benefit of people in Wales
Have governing documents with an asset lock and dividend distribution control
Have independent oversight from a qualified, quorate board of at least three directors or trustees
Have appropriate minimum policy standards in place
Not already started, no land or building purchase, land open to the community, not a regulatory body

documents: Relevant permissions for activity to take place
Signed most recent financial statements or audited annual accounts

status.quote: Current status of the fund The fund is currently closed for applications.

administered_by.quote: The Landfill Disposals Tax Communities Scheme is a Welsh Government grant scheme administered by WCVA.

geography.quote: The Landfill Disposals Tax Communities Scheme will fund projects within five miles of certain waste transfer stations or landfill sites.

access.quote: To apply for the Landfill Disposals Tax Communities Scheme, you will need to register with WCVA's Multipurpose Application Portal (MAP).

amount.quote: Organisations can apply for grants of £5,000 to £49,999 for projects that align with at least one of the scheme's three themes. WCVA may award a grant to one nationally significant project per year, with a value of between £50,000 - £250,000

window.quote: The map will be updated ahead of a funding round opening and will show eligible sites for that round.

co_finance_required.quote: Match funding for the scheme is not required and the scheme can support 100% of project costs.

eligibility.quote: Be an incorporated body based in and operating for the benefit of people in Wales
Have governing documents containing suitable asset lock and dividend distribution control
Have the ability to demonstrate suitable oversight and independence from a qualified and quorate Board with a minimum of three directors or trustees
Have appropriate minimum policy standards in place (eg, safeguarding).
Projects that have already started Purchase of land or buildings Projects on land or a facility that is not accessible to the community within which it is located Regulatory bodies

after_award.quote: the remainder 20% subject to a completed final project report. Monitoring reports will be required every six months.

documents.quote: Signed constitution/governing documents for your organisation (your local County Voluntary Council (CVC) can help you with this if you are a recently formed group) The relevant permissions for activity to take place, see section on land leases and agreements Signed copies of your organisation's most recent financial statements or audited annual accounts
A copy of your organisation's Environmental Policy A copy of your organisation's Equal Opportunities Policy
A scanned/downloaded bank statement to demonstrate that you have a bank account in the name of your group or organisation

effort.quote: There will be a one-stage application process for these grants
Applications will be made through an online grant portal - Multipurpose Application Portal (MAP) - map.wcva.cymru.

steps: One-stage online application on the MAP portal
